name: MAX7219
full_name: Maxim Integrated MAX7219 Serially Interfaced 8-Digit LED Display Driver
description: The MAX7219 is a compact serial driver for up to eight 7-segment digits, an 8x8 LED matrix, or 64 individual LEDs, controlled over a 3-wire SPI-like interface (DIN, CLK, LOAD/CS). It integrates a BCD code-B decoder, multiplex scan circuitry, segment/digit drivers, and an 8x8 static display RAM. A single external resistor on ISET sets the peak segment current for all LEDs, and the DOUT pin lets multiple chips be daisy-chained from one MCU. Its all-in-one design (no external transistors or current-limit resistors per LED) is why it dominates hobbyist 7-segment and matrix builds.

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: serial data input; loaded into the shift register on CLK rising edge

pins.name: GND
pins.description: ground; both GND pins (4 and 9) must be connected

pins.name: GND
pins.description: ground; both GND pins (4 and 9) must be connected

pins.name: LOAD (CS)
pins.description: load/chip-select; the last 16 bits are latched on its rising edge (CS on MAX7221)

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: serial clock input, max 10MHz; data shifts on rising edge

pins.name: ISET
pins.description: peak segment current set; connect resistor (e.g. 9.53k) to V+

pins.name: DOUT
pins.description: serial data output for daisy-chaining; DIN data appears here 16.5 clocks later, never high-Z

extra.drives: 8 x 7-seg digits, or 8x8 LED matrix, or 64 LEDs
extra.brightness: 16 steps, digital (PWM) plus analog via ISET

typical_application: Driving an 8-digit common-cathode 7-segment display or an 8x8 LED matrix from an MCU over 3 wires (DIN, CLK, LOAD), with a single RSET resistor setting brightness; chain modules via DOUT.
gotchas: both GND pins (4 and 9) must be tied to ground, not just one
the DIG and SEG pins are NOT in numeric order on the package (e.g. DIG4 is pin 3, SEG F is pin 15) - follow the datasheet map, not intuition
designed for common-cathode displays; common-anode digits will not work without rewiring
RSET on ISET is mandatory and sets current for all segments; too small a resistor can exceed LED ratings
put a ~10uF + 0.1uF decoupling cap close to V+/GND or the multiplexed switching causes flicker/glitches
MAX7221 is the SPI-compliant, slew-rate-limited (lower EMI) sibling with the same pinout but CS instead of LOAD
